description: Solo team building TerraWhatIf, an interactive astrophysics and planetary climate storytelling simulation powered by NASA open data.
summary:
TerraWhatIf: Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive 3D coastal climate observatory and planetary habitability simulator built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Be An Earth System Trend Detective!"). Instead of reading static climate charts, players walk across a live 3D observatory deck alongside planetary navigator TERRA, scan scientific instruments with a holographic wrist-scanner, test prediction quizzes, and adjust CO2, CH4, orbital distance, and host stars in real time.

Powered by calibrated first-order radiative-balance physics (NASA CERES EBAF) and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression across 2003–2025 NASA Giovanni (MERRA-2 & AIRS) satellite records, TerraWhatIf transforms complex feedbacks—such as Arctic polar amplification, ice-albedo collapse, and runaway greenhouse heating—into immediate 3D visual experiences. By connecting Earth system trends with exoplanet habitability (TRAPPIST-1 e), it helps learners understand why Earth's delicate climate equilibrium matters.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

TerraWhatIf turns planetary climate science into a playable 3D coastal observatory ("Walking 3P" and "Overview" modes). Players follow a 3-chapter narrative mission guided by TERRA, an adaptive AI-inspired companion avatar whose mood responds to planetary conditions:

1. Chapter 1 — The Heat Blanket: Inspect Earth's baseline (+15°C) vs. an airless Earth (-18.5°C), discover how polar ice reflects sunlight, and double CO2 to 560 ppm to observe greenhouse trapping and sea-ice retreat.

2. Chapter 2 — Too Close to the Sun: Predict and test inverse-square stellar flux (1/d²) by pulling Earth to 0.85 AU (+38% sunlight) and triggering Clausius-Clapeyron water-vapor feedback.

3. Chapter 3 — Red Sun TRAPPIST-1: Switch the host star from our Sun (5772 K) to red dwarf TRAPPIST-1 (2566 K), locate the Kopparapu Habitable Zone (~0.029 AU), and explore Rayleigh sunset-amber skies and tidal-locked day-night terminators.

KEY FEATURES & CREATIVITY

- 3-Layer "Touch to Understand" Cards: Every deck landmark opens three progressive learning tabs—Look! (3D visual cues), Why? (everyday analogies), and Math & NASA Data (live equations, optical-depth breakdown, and NASA observations).

- Real NASA Satellite Trend Engine & 3D Replay: Computes OLS slope per decade, R², t-statistic, p-value, and 95% confidence intervals across 2003–2025 MERRA-2 and AIRS series, with animated sparklines and a "Play 2003→2025 in 3D" replay mode directly inside the observatory.

- Instant "What-If" Lab & Gamification: Includes 1-click presets (Earth Today, Snowball Earth, 2× CO2 Future, Runaway Heat, TRAPPIST-1 e), live "vs. Earth" delta readouts, prediction quizzes, 5 Detective Badges, and an open Science Lab sandbox transparently documenting model scope and limitations.

- Procedural Web Audio & Zero-Asset Visuals: All soundscapes, chapter music, comms typing ticks, 15-wavelength Rayleigh sky colors, 3D weather particles (snow flurries & thermal embers), and the 3D mini Habitable Zone hologram are synthesized procedurally in the browser.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Climate data is often locked behind dense spreadsheets or abstract graphs. TerraWhatIf bridges the gap between rigorous NASA Earth-system datasets and intuitive spatial curiosity—helping students, educators, and citizen scientists grasp cause-and-effect feedbacks in seconds rather than hours.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SCIENTIFIC CALIBRATION

- Frontend & 3D: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Three.js (WebGLRenderer, ACESFilmicToneMapping, OrbitControls), Lucide React.

- Physics & Statistics Engine: Custom zero-dependency ES modules solving radiative equilibrium, hyperbolic-tangent ice-albedo coupling, damped fixed-point infrared optical depth iteration, Kopparapu et al. (2013) Habitable Zone boundaries, and Student's t-test OLS regression—verified by a 10-assertion calibration test suite against NASA CERES EBAF.

- Audio: Procedural Web Audio API synthesizer (no external copyrighted audio tracks).

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS & SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

We prioritized accessibility (keyboard shortcuts, mobile touch D-Pad, reduced-motion support, and jargon-free explanations alongside full equations) and strict scientific transparency.

- Code & Data Disclosure: Large Language Model / Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used to accelerate TypeScript/Three.js code development and to compile/structure the 2003–2025 NASA Giovanni benchmark time series (modeled on authentic MERRA-2 & AIRS climatological records) and NASA Exoplanet Archive TRAPPIST-1 parameters.

- Audio/Video Disclosure: If AI-assisted video editing or text-to-speech tools were used in preparing the 30-second demo video, they are acknowledged in the video description/metadata without using or modifying NASA logos or branding.
